newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty says Israel is holding Lebanese as pawns.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says Israel is holding Lebanese as pawns.

text.p: Amnesty International accused Israel on Thursday of unlawfully holding Lebanese nationals to use as a bargaining chip with Islamic militia groups.
The human rights organisation said some detainees had been held without charge or trial, and with no information on when they will be released, for up to 12 years.
"It is unacceptable that a state should continue to hold human beings as pawns, outside any legal framework," Amnesty said in a statement.
"Those captured and held in Israel and South Lebanon are being held as hostages by the state of Israel to be used a human bargaining chip with Islamist militia groups."
In a report entitled "Israel's Forgotten Hostages," Amnesty detailed the case of 21 Lebanese whom it claims were abducted in their own country and secretly moved to Israel.
It also said more than 130 other Lebanese were held in Khiam detention centre which is run by the South Lebanon Army (SLA) in a security zone Israel occupies in South Lebanon.
Amnesty said the Israeli government and the SLA had stated that the freedom of the detainees was conditional on the release or information about Israeli soldiers missing in Lebanon.
The group also disputes Israel's claim that the people detained are terrorists and are being held legally.
"Laws...which allow people to be detained for years after the expiry of their sentences and without trial violate their fundamental human rights," Amnesty said.
"Those accused of terrorism have the right to be brought to fair trial. If the Israeli government is not prepared to do this the detainees should be immediately freed."
Amnesty said it sent a memorandum to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in March about the cases featured in its report but had not received a reply.
